rule: Three tunable layers. (A) Landmark overmap specials carry occurrence and city-distance weights and, for camps and nests, a population and radius block. (B) Monstergroups carry budget points per member (cost_multiplier), pack-size ranges and day or season windows. (C) Ambient walk density: per-terrain spawns chance (percent) times a world SPAWN_DENSITY knob; population per tile is a count times rng(min,max). Timed roadstop encounters roll every 1800 recurrence with a 10 percent chance and a 7-day spawn tag. Roadblocks are road map extras that nest one or two chunks, place 0-2 vehicles and 0-2 monsters, and sometimes place nothing.

change: Camp rosters up to 14 NPCs: cap on-screen attackers at 3 and keep the rest as a reserve pool.
Ambient rolls run inside the single game process in the donor; in ours every roll and respawn runs on the server and the client only shows the result.
Characters come from the 100-Pit family pool by family id, not from per-zone content.
Art, names and palette: original, not the donor's glyphs or lore.
look_test: Static flag on the existing scene, no release rows. Three 375-wide screens with the same three enemy sprites: (1) a 2x2 walled camp with a roof layer and three members at the gate; (2) a red X marker on a road tile with two members behind a vehicle sprite, visible for six tiles; (3) a web-patch lair with two members and no marker until the last tile. Dom judges: count of attackers at a glance, whether the marker reads before contact, whether the lair says stay out in one look. Then compare the density knob at 0.5x, 1x and 2x on one 60-second walk loop (not built).
